$comment: Every entry names a test and the ONE-LINE change to production source that must
make it go red. `make test-mutation` applies each change, runs the named gate,
and fails if the gate still passes — because a test that survives the deletion of
the code it claims to pin is asserting something else.
This exists because three tests landed in #321 that passed for the wrong reason,
and every one was caught by doing this by hand: an oracle case that threw inside
its own setup and so printed identical output on both runtimes, a property suite
that compared zero inputs after a NaN run count, and an event-loop test whose
timer handed platform_poll a positive timeout, which counts as progress by itself
and so never produced the no-progress tick under test. Doing it by hand depends on
remembering to; this does not.
Fields:
name    what the mutation proves, in the form '<test> dies when <code> is broken'
why     one sentence: the defect this catches if the mutation survives
source  production file to patch (never a test file)
find    exact string to replace; must appear EXACTLY once (the runner checks)
replace what to put there — usually the pre-fix code, or a deleted guard
gate    how to observe red; see GATE KINDS in scripts/run-mutations.mjs
expect_detail  substring the RED output must contain; '' is a visible opt-out
(`rebuild` is gone: it was derivable from the gate kind, and a run filtered to
only `make:` entries then skipped the restore build and left bin/lava holding
the mutated source with a clean git tree and a success message.)

mutations.name: 55-encoding-pollution V dies when the utf-8 decode return path goes back through .call
mutations.why: A replaced Function.prototype.call substitutes decode()'s return value outright, so decode() hands back an ArrayBuffer instead of a string.

mutations.name: 55-encoding-pollution U dies when toBytes reads the view window live
mutations.why: A poisoned byteOffset/byteLength pair selects a window across the shared allocUnsafe pool, so decode() returns a neighbouring Buffer's bytes.

mutations.name: 55-encoding-pollution W dies when toBytes brands with instanceof
mutations.why: Ctor[Symbol.hasInstance] is a configurable own property, so the brand is forgeable in both directions and misroutes the input into the wrong arm.

mutations.name: 13-structured-clone dies when the DataView clone arm reads its window live
mutations.why: structuredClone copies the whole backing buffer and re-slices the copy, so a poisoned window exposes pool neighbours in the clone.
mutations.expect_detail: DataView clone window must not widen under a poisoned getter

mutations.name: 13-structured-clone dies when the DataView brand goes back to instanceof
mutations.why: A forged DataView[Symbol.hasInstance] misroutes a genuine DataView into the typed-array arm, where the captured getter rejects the receiver.
mutations.expect_detail: a forged hasInstance must not break a real DataView clone

mutations.name: run_until_idle_waits_out_a_stale_wakeup dies when a no-progress tick ends the drive
mutations.why: A surplus wakeup byte ends the drive with an off-loop completion still in flight, and it returns the did_work an earlier tick latched — so it reports success.

mutations.name: the detector's fixtures die when isWrite swallows read-modify-write again
mutations.why: Compound, logical and update assignments all run GetValue before PutValue, so exempting them lets the ratchet pay out for rewriting a counted read as `??=`.

mutations.name: the detector's fixtures die when the Identifier visitor's params guard is removed
mutations.why: PropertyDefinition is in FUNCTION_TYPES but has no .params, so `class C { x = String; }` crashed the whole scan on valid syntax.
mutations.expect_detail: class field holding a bare global reference

mutations.name: the baseline tests die when the per-class comparison collapses into a total
mutations.why: A file that fixes one accessor and gains one live global has an unchanged total, and per-class baselines exist precisely so that cannot pass.

mutations.name: the poisoned http-smoke phases die when a framing validator goes back to re.test
mutations.why: Content-Length framing. With the check on a live regex, a poisoned exec answered 200 OK for `Content-Length: abc` — parseInt gives NaN and the body framing desyncs. The charCode form has no regex to poison at all.

mutations.name: the poisoned http-smoke phases die when the chunked check goes back to re.test
mutations.why: Transfer-Encoding framing. A steered check accepted `gzip` as chunked, which is the other half of the smuggling pair.

mutations.name: the runner's own tests die when SURVIVED is not reported
mutations.why: Inverting this branch makes every surviving mutation read as a kill, which is the exact P0 a review found: a gate whose value is its honesty, with nothing checking that honesty.

mutations.name: the runner's own tests die when WRONG REASON stops being enforced
mutations.why: This branch IS 82d8a0e. Without it a mutation that breaks something unrelated is reported as killed, which is how a mis-escaped replacement once looked like it worked.

mutations.name: the runner's own tests die when the green-baseline check is removed
mutations.why: Without it the gate reports a kill for a target that was already failing, so 'it went red' proves nothing.

mutations.name: the runner's own tests die when a stale entry becomes a silent skip
mutations.why: A manifest entry that no longer describes the code must fail; skipping it drops the coverage the gate exists to guarantee.

mutations.name: 54-url-pollution X1 dies when endsInANumber goes back to a live re.test
mutations.why: Steered true, '4x' reads as numeric and parseInt gives 4, so http://1.2.3.4x/ silently becomes http://1.2.3.4/ — a host substitution.

mutations.name: 54-url-pollution X2 dies when the %2f check goes back to a live re.test
mutations.why: The path-traversal guard, in the direction that discriminates: a steered validator makes a legitimate path look encoded and throws where node returns one.

mutations.name: the Lava-only regexp pollution test dies when the header-name validator goes back to re.test
mutations.why: node ACCEPTS 'X-Evil: 1\r\nInjected' under this poison (undici's validator is JS), so this deviation cannot be oracled and CLAUDE.md section 1 requires a Lava-only pin.

mutations.name: the Lava-only regexp pollution test dies when the header trim goes back to a global replaceAll
mutations.why: A global replace under a forged exec does not answer wrongly — it never returns, because lastIndex only advances on an empty match. The observable effect IS the hang, so the recorded reason is the timeout verdict: before capture() bounded it this entry ate 3m16s and multi-GB in CI and degraded to WRONG REASON on a memory-capped runner.

mutations.name: 57-format-single-arg dies when util.js drops the single-argument guard
mutations.why: Without it util.format folds %% even with one argument, where node returns the string verbatim. Pinned separately from console.js because the two are different implementations and one entry would fake coverage of both.

mutations.name: 57-format-single-arg dies when console.js drops the single-argument guard
mutations.why: console.js has its own formatter — it is the bootstrap prelude and has no require to delegate with — so removing util.js's guard leaves console.log correct and vice versa. This entry moves the raw console.log rows, a different line range from the util entry.

mutations.name: the Lava-only test dies when the header-value scan reads charCodeAt live
mutations.why: Routing the validator off RegExp says nothing about what it scans WITH. A gadget lying only about CR/LF made Lava accept 'a\r\nInjected: yes' as a header value where node rejects, and turned res.setHeader('Location', decodeURIComponent(req.url)) into a split response from a remote request line.

mutations.name: the Lava-only test dies when normalizeBase64 goes back to a global replace
mutations.why: A global replace under a forged exec never terminates. Buffer.from(x,'base64') is the Basic-auth/JWT path, so one unauthenticated request with an Authorization header wedged the event loop for good. The observable effect of this mutation IS the hang, so the recorded reason is the timeout verdict rather than a message: a spin produces no error text. The three spin entries share that detail by construction and are discriminated by `source`/`find` — each is applied on its own run, so the file named in the entry is the one that hung.

mutations.name: the Lava-only test dies when toUSVString goes back to the global regex
mutations.why: The surrogate pre-scan is not a guard against this: a VALID pair — any emoji in a remote query — sets hasSurrogate too, and the global replace then spins. new URLSearchParams(remoteQuery) is on the network path. The observable effect of this mutation IS the hang, so the recorded reason is the timeout verdict rather than a message: a spin produces no error text. The three spin entries share that detail by construction and are discriminated by `source`/`find` — each is applied on its own run, so the file named in the entry is the one that hung.
